subject: Re: MAP review — token/cost assumptions and eval timeline
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@prefectai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-23T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: MAP kickoff — cost assumptions + eval plan

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for sending the MAP template last week. We're starting to map out the evaluation and close timeline and need a sanity check on the cost / unit-econ assumptions before we lock any commitments. High level asks:

- Can you confirm tokens per request and tokens/$ for the recommended model (redwood-8k-quant)? We run a two-step flow: short user query (avg 18 tokens), long context doc retrieval + summarization (avg 1,200 tokens) and a final synthesis prompt (avg 320 tokens).
- What's your recommended batching size and expected latency impact (p95) for interactive demo traffic vs background batch eval?
- Any cache/prefetch guidance (prefix vs full-KV) that would materially change token consumption?
- We need an eval plan that fits a 6-week pilot with an aim to close by 2026-08-15 if metrics look good.

Attached is our provisional success criteria doc — we'll share more after our internal sync. Can you return a MAP with explicit cost sensitivity (tokens/$) and a short canary evaluation plan that ties to close milestones?

Appreciate the quick turn on this.

—Maya
Maya Singh
Director, AI Systems
PrefectAI

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost assumptions + eval plan

Maya — thanks, and great context. I'm attaching a MAP draft (v1) and a short cost sensitivity spreadsheet. Key summary below; I'll loop Ben & Karthik for a quick ops sanity check.

High-level assumptions (initial):
- Recommended model: redwood-8k-quant (4-bit quant, KV-friendly).
- Baseline tokens/request: 1,538 tokens avg (query 18 + retrieval 1,200 + synth 320).
- Estimated tokens per 1,000 requests: ~1.54M tokens.
- Baseline price: $0.0009 per token (hosted, quantized tier) => $1,384 per 1M tokens => projected $2,129 / 1,000 requests.
- Batching: suggested interactive batching window 15–25ms (batch size ~8) to keep p95 latency under 350ms in hosted; background evals can batch up to 128 for cost efficiency.
- Caching: prefix caching on retrieval summaries (cacheable ~40% of flows) can reduce compute tokens by ~28% for repeat queries; full-KV caching recommended for long-form sessions with warm state.

Proposed 6-week eval plan (canary -> scale):
1) Week 0: Baseline telemetry capture + seeded prompts (run 1k requests/day).
2) Week 1–2: Canary with 5% traffic routed to redwood-8k-quant; collect latency/cost/quality and run A/B on prompt shorteners.
3) Week 3–4: Scale to 25% traffic; enable prefix caching and measure token delta.
4) Week 5–6: Full pilot; run heavy eval (50k synthetic requests) and cost stress scenarios.

Deliverables: updated MAP (v2) with final tokens/$ table, cost sensitivity scenarios, recommended batching config, and rollout steps.

Ben/Karthik — can you validate the tokens/$ calc and call out any infra constraints for prefix caching and canary batch sizes?

Thanks,
Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-23T14:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — cost assumptions + eval plan (internal)

Steph / Karthik — quick ops sanity check from the runtime side. Notes:

1) Tokens per request: the 1,538 estimate is reasonable as a high-level number, but we should provision for a 15–25% delta depending on retrieval size variance and user-added context. In practice for PrefectAI sample corpus we saw median retrieval size closer to 1,400 tokens but 75th percentile ~1,700. Recommend we model conservative and optimistic scenarios.

2) Batching & latency: interactive batching size of 8 with a 20ms hold is fine on hosted. However, p95 will be dominated by serialization + cold KV loads for first-time retrievals; expect p95 bump of ~120–160ms for cold traffic. For canary, plan to route traffic from a small set of users (consistent IDs) so we can warm caches quickly.

3) Caching: prefix caching assumptions are solid. For this flow, we should treat retrieval summaries as cacheable keys. Expect ~25–35% token savings when cache hit rate is >40%. Memory/GPUs: full-KV caching at scale will require additional GPU memory reservations (estimate +1x GPU per 40k concurrent warm sessions). Call this out as a risk if they want aggressive full-KV.

4) Cost math check: cost numbers look OK, but note that quantized hosted tiers sometimes have tiered pricing for high-throughput sustained commits. If PrefectAI intends sustained 1M+ tokens/month, we should present a reserved capacity delta.

I'll update the cost sensitivity sheet with 3 scenarios (optimistic/expected/conservative) and the per-request token ranges.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Maya — thanks for the patience. We've reconciled the MAP and attached v2 plus the sensitivity workbook (tabbed optimistic/expected/conservative). Summary of the reconciled economics and recommended next steps: 

- Per-request tokens (final ranges): optimistic 1,250 | expected 1,540 | conservative 1,925.
- Tokens per 1k requests: opt 1.25M | exp 1.54M | cons 1.93M.
- Price per token (hosted quant tier): $0.00085 (volume-adjusted scenario available for committed reserved capacity).
- Cost per 1k requests (expected): ~ $1,309 (expected) — this factors in a 30% cache hit rate and moderate batching. Conservative cost per 1k: ~$1,636.

Recommended MAP gating for your 6-week pilot to align to close by 2026-08-15: 
1) Sign MAP v2 and provision canary (Week 0).
2) Week 1–2: 5% traffic canary + prefix caching enabled for warm cohort. Checkpoint: token delta <20% vs expected, latency p95 <500ms.
3) Week 3–4: Expand to 25% traffic, enable background batching for eval workloads. Checkpoint: cost trend vs model within +/-10%.
4) Week 5–6: Full pilot and business review; if cost/quality gates met, execute reserved capacity quote and finalize SOW.

Next steps: 1) Are you available Thu 6/25 10:00am ET for a 30-min alignment to finalize the MAP and pick the canary cohort? 2) I'll attach committed-capacity pricing options if you think you'll hit >1M tokens/month.

Attachments: MAP-draft-v2.pdf (pdf), cost-sensitivity-sheet.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

—Steph
